capabilities.label: Functions, parameters, return types, and scalar arithmetic
capabilities.limitations: Int is signed 64-bit with checked arithmetic, deterministic overflow and zero-divisor errors, and truncation-toward-zero division/remainder (docs/language/native-numeric-contract.md; native.rs source-to-native edge tests). Scalar float arithmetic, casts/conversions, NaN/Infinity policy, and complete Rust numeric/type-system parity remain unestablished.

capabilities.label: User-defined structs, enums, and exhaustive pattern matching
Trait constraints, impl blocks, and generic function/type checking
Flow-sensitive ownership, borrowing, lifetime regions, and drop
capabilities.limitations: Existing analysis does not establish full Rust-compatible soundness.

capabilities.label: Option, Result, propagation, and error conversions
capabilities.limitations: Full Option and propagation/conversion semantics are not established.

capabilities.label: UTF-8 byte strings, Unicode scalar/grapheme access, safe string slices, typed lists, and owned list slices
capabilities.limitations: String[index] remains UTF-8 byte indexing; String[start:end] returns an owned copy and requires scalar boundaries. scalar_len/scalar_at operate on Unicode scalar values; grapheme_len/grapheme_at use pinned unicode-segmentation 1.12.0 extended grapheme clusters. Iterator protocol/syntax, borrowed views, full flow-sensitive Rust ownership/lifetime/drop parity, and Rust standard-library parity remain unsupported or unproven.

capabilities.label: Closures, capture modes, iterators, and for loops
capabilities.limitations: The native compiler supports a bounded source-level for/in subset over List<T> through deterministic index-based lowering. This does not implement iterator traits, closures/capture modes, break/continue, full Rust ownership/lifetime/drop parity, or self-hosting. Differential/holdout and Stage 2/3 reproducibility remain independent promotion gates.

capabilities.label: Rust async/await and Future semantics
capabilities.limitations: Rust async/await, Future polling, pinning and async cancellation are intentionally unsupported and tested fail-closed. The narrower structured spawn/join/cancel model is not equivalent; see docs/language/concurrency-contract.md.

capabilities.label: Modules, visibility, package resolution, and reproducible dependencies
capabilities.limitations: Rust crate and Cargo compatibility is not established.

capabilities.label: Macros, const generics, attributes/cfg, unsafe, broad FFI, and custom targets
Source-level threads, atomics, locks, and memory ordering
capabilities.limitations: Ardisa exposes no native source-level atomic, mutex, lock, channel, or memory-ordering operations. Internal host Rust synchronization is not language support. The structured task subset does not establish shared-memory race freedom or Rust memory-ordering parity; see docs/language/synchronization-contract.md.
